results.summary_before: This project is a simplified memory controller that simulates DRAM read/write behavior with request queuing, bank-row-column address decoding, and a fake memory. It services requests from a testbench CPU in order, using a bank table to track open rows, though the final design includes only one bank, two rows, and two columns to reduce area. The controller runs at 50 MHz and has a defined interface for read and write transactions. Testing was done with SystemVerilog testbenches and cocotb, and no external hardware is needed.

results.summary_before: TinyCrypto-8 is an 8-bit pipelined ALU with hardware cryptography support, featuring a 12-bit instruction set that includes arithmetic, logic, shift, and LFSR-based crypto operations. Instructions are loaded serially through three input pins, and the 8-bit accumulator result is output on eight pins. The design is verified with a testbench that exercises ALU operations, flag updates, and crypto functions, and it requires no external hardware for basic operation. It is intended for educational or integration purposes, with optional microcontroller-based testing.

results.summary_before: This design is an 8-channel programmable clock router that generates divided clock signals from a 50 MHz system clock. Each output channel can be independently configured via a 3-bit address, 4-bit division value, and a write strobe to select one of 16 counter bits as the clock source. The outputs are directly observable with a logic analyzer or oscilloscope, and no external hardware is required. The design is a straightforward utility for clock management in digital systems.

results.summary_before: This project implements a ring oscillator physical unclonable function (RO-PUF) using 16 toggle flip-flops driven by an LFSR to create unique oscillators. Eight 12-bit counter pairs measure frequency variations over a 1000-cycle window, and a three-state FSM manages the measurement cycle, producing a single-bit response and a done flag. The design requires no external hardware and outputs debug information on six pins. It is notable for exploiting silicon manufacturing variation for hardware security primitives.

results.summary_before: SandSim is a SystemVerilog physics engine that simulates falling sand on a 36x48 binary grid, computing the next state for pairs of rows with a compute kernel. It outputs a 640x480-style VGA signal through the Tiny VGA pinout and stores data in external QSPI flash and RAM. Users drive any of the eight ui pins high to spawn a grain of sand at the top of the grid. It requires a TinyVGA Pmod and a TinyQSPI Pmod to operate.

results.summary_before: This is a UART-controlled smart I/O hub built around a 64-channel PWM engine, with channels divided into banks of eight selected by ui_in[6:4]. UART commands can write duty cycles, set a prescaler, and load internal modulation registers, while the upper eight channels are driven by a phase counter, an LFSR-style pattern source and an add/multiply datapath. A status page can be shown on uio_out when ui_in[7] is asserted, and a sequencer enable and clear-registers input are provided. It requires a USB-to-UART adapter or microcontroller and an oscilloscope or logic analyzer, and the pinout matches the TT Audio recommendation.
